title: Residential exhaust outlet clearance from air intakes
purpose: Provides an alternative solution to Sentence 9.32.3.13.(4) for the minimum clearance requirement for domestic exhaust outlets that discharge air containing moisture, such as kitchen, bathroom, and clothes dryer exhaust outlets, from air intakes.
discussion: The National Building Code of Canada 2020 introduced changes to Article 9.32.3.13. for minimum clearance requirements related to exhaust vents, soffits, and air intakes. The National Building Code – 2023 Alberta Edition (NBC(AE)) subsequently harmonized with these changes. The minimum clearance required between a gas vent or oil fill pipe and a mechanically vented air intake was increased from 900 mm to 1 800 mm in Sentence 9.32.3.13.(3). Additionally, new Sentences (4) to (6) were introduced to address the minimum clearance required from exhaust outlets discharging moisture-laden air to soffits and air intakes. While the national code change rationale for Sentences (4) to (6) specifically explained the application of the 1 800 mm minimum clearance requirement to soffits, it did not address the application to air intakes as provided in Sentence (4). A required 1 800 mm minimum clearance between moist-air exhaust outlets and air intakes for domestic applications was not explained and other standards suggest it can be potentially reduced. CSA-B149.1, “Natural gas and propane installation code,” (CSA B149.1) provides minimum clearances between clothes dryer vent terminations and air intakes: 900 mm for domestic clothes dryers and 1 800 mm for commercial clothes dryers. As domestic clothes dryer exhaust air typically contains more moisture than bathroom or kitchen exhaust air, this supports the basis for a variance that reduces the 1 800 mm minimum required clearance between a moist-air exhaust outlet and air intake specified by Sentence 9.32.3.13.(4) of the NBC(AE). As air intakes located above moist-air exhaust outlets are more susceptible to the effects of infiltration (due to the rising of warm, moist air), the reduction in the required minimum clearance from 1 800 mm to 900 mm provided in this variance is only applicable to where the moist-air exhaust outlet is located horizontally to the air intake or above it. This maintains the rationale for the changes to Article 9.32.3.13. in the NBC(AE) while providing appropriate reductions in the required minimum clearance for certain dimensions (see Figure A). Air intakes specified by Sentence (4) refer to intakes supplying ventilation air to the building and includes those connected to HRV’s/ERV’s or the return air plenum of a furnace. Note that in cases where the fresh air intake connected to the return air plenum of a furnace is less than 8 inches in diameter, it can be considered as a “building opening” rather than an air intake (as the CSA B149.1 standard also allows for). Moist-air exhaust outlets specified by Sentence (4) include not only bathroom ventilation and clothes dryer exhaust outlets, but kitchen exhaust outlets as well, despite kitchen exhaust outlets not being explicitly mentioned in the Sentence itself or in the rationale for the code change. It is important to note that where the minimum clearance requirements contained within a manufacturer’s installation instructions differ from the Code or this STANDATA, the more stringent requirements apply.

applies_to: This variance applies to exhaust outlets that discharge air containing moisture, such as kitchen, bathroom and clothes dryer exhaust outlets, serving an individual dwelling unit or a house with a secondary suite.
